title: Small-batch unstick and cohort warmup lab notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes for a small-batch 'unstick' flow and cohort warmup sequence. This is a personal scratchpad: half procedural, half heuristics. Use as a starting template for staging runs. Not final — lots of TODOs and open questions at the end.

Context / when to use:
- Use when a rollout has stalled (traffic fraction plateau, or client SDKs not picking up new variant) and we want a low-risk, repeatable way to re-prime traffic without wide rollbacks.
- Also helpful for pre-warm of model variants that have cold caches or KV cache priming needs (RPS-sensitive).

Goals:
1) Restore steady ramp to target fraction with < 5% error-rate delta vs baseline.
2) Avoid noisy broad rollbacks; prefer micro-cohort probes + synthetic priming.
3) Keep cost delta bounded (watch GPU burst minutes and token spend during warmup).

Constraints / guardrails:
- Max extra traffic for synthetic priming: 2% of peak for any 10m window (budget control).
- If latency p50 increases > 20% or p95 > 40% relative to baseline for 10m, abort and pinback.
- No change to client-visible model version mapping without CS approval for tenants in regulatory cohort.

High-level sequence (small-batch unstick):
1) Identify stuck cohort(s): clients with repeated 429/timeout or low conversion after flip. Query: "count by (client_id) (increase(requests[30m])) and error_rate(client_id)" — pick top 3 offenders.
2) Shadow prime: route synthetic priming traffic (simple short prompts) to the variant behind a shadowed flag for 15m at 0.25% of overall traffic. Validate KV cache fill / initial token cost.
3) Micro-cohort probe: enable variant for 0.5% of live traffic but limit to users in the above cohorts (client affinity routing). 10m window. Collect metrics: latency (p50/p95), error_rate, token cost, quality score (if available).
4) Expand in linear micro-steps: 0.5 -> 1.5 -> 3% spaced 10–15m apart. At each step, run heatchecks (see 'heatcheck checklist' below). If any step fails, pinback to previous stable fraction and run synthetic re-prime for 20m.
5) Full warmup: once 3% shows stable metrics for 30m, bump to 10% with an intermediate synthetic priming burst (1% for 5m).
6) Resume normal rollout cadence (day-of-week and region-aware).

Heatcheck checklist (on each expansion step):
- Latency: p50 change < +15% and p95 change < +30% vs baseline
- Error rate: < baseline + 0.5 percentage points or absolute < 1% (whichever stricter)
- Token spend rate: within expected trend line for the cohort
- Model quality: sampling-based metric (top-100 prompts) no regression > 2%
- Observability: no spike in infra OOMs, GPU error counts, or scheduler preemption events
- Alerts: no new Sev2/Sev1 alerts triggered in the window

Pinned fallback / pinback policy (quick):
- Immediate pinback if p95 latency > 2x baseline or if error_rate > 3% for any 5m window.
- Soft pinback (reduce fractional traffic by 50%) if p95 > 1.5x baseline OR if quality-sampling drops between 2–4% for 20m.
- Hard pinback to previous stable image if soft pinback does not recover in 20m.

Telemetry queries / quick references:
- Live cohort error rate (PromQL):
  sum(rate(request_errors_total{stage="serve",variant=~"new.*"}[5m])) by (client_id) / sum(rate(requests_total{stage="serve",variant=~"new.*"}[5m])) by (client_id)
- KV cache hit ratio (by node):
  sum(kv_cache_hits_total{variant="new"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups_total{variant="new"})
- GPU burst minutes (billing):
  increase(gpu_burst_minutes_total[1h])
- Synthetic priming success (simple heuristic): synthetic_responses{status="ok"} / synthetic_responses_total

Quick rollback/playbook snippets:
- API toggle (release service): curl -X POST https://release.redwood.internal/api/v1/route-toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/api/generate","variant":"new","fraction":0.005}'
- Pinback via rollout-service: auth and then POST /rollouts/{id}/pin-back with body {"target_fraction":0.0} (team script: scripts/pinback.sh)
- K8s emergency rollback (only if release control plane unreachable): kubectl -n production set image deploy/gateway gateway=image:stable-20250201 && kubectl rollout restart deploy/gateway

Synthetic priming recipes (cheap short prompts):
- Short-context permutations: 6–12 tokens prompts that exercise model embedding and kv cache paths. Eg: "Summarize: cat photos" variations.
- Slot-filling microrequests to heat tokenizer/kvcache: use dataset of 300 seeds per region. Keep each request < 40 tokens.

Cost considerations:
- Track "priming cost" separately for the rollout (label usage: rollout_id=RINF-724). Expect extra token spend of ~0.2–0.6% of daily budget for full warmup per variant.
- Watch GPU preemption events which cause re-priming loops and cost amplification.

Client communication and CS coordination:
- If cohort includes enterprise tenants with dedicated contracts, loop in CS 30–60m pre action. Slack channel: #cs-unstick.
- Prepare two canned messages: (1) brief heads-up (scheduled warmup), (2) incident message if we pinback or rollback.

Preflight checklist (before starting micro-probes):
- [ ] Confirm baseline metrics snapshot (p50/p95/err rate) and save to confluence page link above
- [ ] Create ephemeral monitoring dashboard for the cohort (copy template: /dashboards/unstick-template)
- [ ] Ensure oncall and release-owner are aware and on standby
- [ ] Attach rollout_id tag to all synthetic priming traffic and logs
- [ ] Approve budget with finance if expected extra GPU minutes > threshold

Post-run notes template (fill after run):
- Run id: RINF-
- Start/end times:
- Cohorts targeted:
- Max fraction reached:
- Number of expansion steps and durations:
- Any pinbacks and reasons:
- Telemetry summary (attach CSV): latency, error, token spend
- Cost incurred estimate:
- Follow-ups / next steps:

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to better detect 'unstick' root cause vs client-side throttles? Need client SDK telemetry. Add request-level headers to signal SDK version.
- Should we have an automated 'soft nudge' (client-side header priority bump) that slightly biases client SDK traffic during warmup? Privacy and contract implications.
- A/B quality sampling: can we automate sampling checks per cohort (GitHub PR exists but needs owner).
- Add synthetic priming job to the release control plane so it can be scheduled as part of rollout (ops cost + safety review required).

Notes to self:
- Keep micro-steps short and deterministic. Avoid human intuition scaling too large.
- If one region shows persistent high p95, isolate region and run region-only warmup with synthetic priming at 0.5% first.
- Remember: sometimes the "unstick" is just a caching TTL mismatch; check edge-cache logs before expanding traffic.

End of scratchpad.
